proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 is a high-level pointwise-CATE upper theorem requiring trained nuisance and covariate-law estimators, bounded Gram eigenvalues, basis approximation, and a uniform density-ratio condition; the present result matches its algebraic three-term objective under an alternative primitive-law package.
Theorem 1 studies same-sample stabilized empirical HOIFs for global bilinear forms; that theorem is not imported into the local causal proof.
The paper develops an independent-sample empirical-Gram HOIF construction; no projection-stability claim from it is used here.
Section 2, Theorem 2.1 analyzes a two-scale contrast for homoskedastic variance, not the causal pair numerator and denominator proved here.
The pointwise variance theorem analyzes a pairwise-difference statistic under random design, while the present causal identity and collision bounds are derived directly.
The paper establishes doubly robust confidence bands in a first-order local-smoothing regime.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The new optimizer corollary and positive-band converse distinguish algebraic objective attainment from KBRW's alternative high-level upper-theorem hypotheses and support-hole lower-bound construction.

prose_updates.tldr: On \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}=\{0<\alpha,\beta,\gamma\leq1\}\), one bounded density-free cross-pair estimator attains the optimizer-defined three-term objective without logarithmic loss.  With \(s=(\alpha+\beta)/2\) and \(s_0=d\gamma/\{2(2\gamma+d)\}\), that objective has order \(n^{-1/\{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s)\}}\) below the elbow and \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) at and above it.  A uniform-design Bernoulli two-point submodel proves the positive-band lower rate \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), so the latter is the positive-band minimax rate when \(s\geq s_0\).  Below the elbow the former is an attained upper benchmark, while a matching positive-band converse remains unresolved.  The order-one region includes \(U=\{0<\alpha<\beta<\gamma<1\}\) outside the banked region.

project_justification.gap: The algebraic three-term KBRW objective was not accompanied by a proof that the present density-free cross-pair estimator attains it on the fixed positive-band class, nor by a positive-band converse.  The published low-smoothness hard laws use density support holes, so they cannot settle the below-elbow minimax rate on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band}}\).
project_justification.niche: On the explicitly restricted positive-band class and \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\), close pairs provide the local mass \(h^{2d}/k\) needed for an order-one product remainder.  Overlap supplies a deterministic population denominator margin, while direct overlap-graph counting controls the diagonal and one-shared-index variance terms of the proved order-one pair kernel.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the explicit screened cross-pair upper bound, directly minimizes its three-term oracle objective with integer tuning, and supplies a uniform-design Bernoulli two-point lower bound inside the positive-band class.  This closes the positive-band minimax rate at and above the elbow and gives an honest upper/lower bracket below it, without density estimation or logarithmic loss.

prose_updates.related_work: CausalSmith attains the algebraic three-term objective appearing in KBRW on the fixed positive-band class and \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\).  KBRW Theorem 2 is instead a high-level upper theorem requiring trained nuisance and covariate-law estimators, bounded Gram eigenvalues, basis approximation, and a uniform density-ratio condition, so its full hypothesis package and the present primitive-law package are alternative regimes rather than nested theorem classes.  At the law level \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band}}\) is a restricted positive-density submodel of KBRW's broad smooth model where the parametrizations overlap, but KBRW's low-smoothness hard densities have support holes; hence that converse does not transfer.  The standard uniform-design regression submodel does transfer the oracle lower bound.  Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020) and Dobriban, Mukherjee, Robins, and Wang (2026) motivate close-pair contrasts for noncausal variance problems, but neither source proves the causal numerator/denominator identity used here.  Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2017) and Liu, Li, Gu, and Liu (2026) concern empirical-Gram or stabilized HOIF constructions; no projection, spectral, or M\"obius theorem from those papers is imported.
prose_updates.interpretation: The optimizer has an explicit elbow at \(s_0=d\gamma/\{2(2\gamma+d)\}\).  Below it, balancing localization, the product remainder, and the pair-collision term gives \(r_n^*\asymp n^{-1/\{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(4s)\}}\); this is an attained upper benchmark, not a proved positive-band minimax rate.  At and above the elbow, \(k\asymp nh^d\) and \(h\asymp n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)}\) give \(r_n^*\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), matching the positive-band two-point lower bound.  Both deterministic labels invoke the same total cross-pair map.  Any KBRW benchmark comparison outside \(\gamma\geq\beta\) is only an algebraic continuation of the objective, not a transfer of KBRW's full theorem class.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The proved estimator is order one and attains the unsaturated objective only on \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\); its all-smoothness robustness bound saturates every first-difference exponent at one.  Any higher-order extension beyond \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\) would require an explicitly specified random-design contrast or localized M\"obius estimator together with the corresponding projection or normalization bounds, causal numerator/denominator expansion, exceptional-event control, and complete higher-order collision/Hoeffding accounting.  None is asserted here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Identification is given by the frozen CATE identification lemma.  The note proves the oracle positive-band lower bound and hence minimax optimality above the elbow.  It does not prove a matching positive-band converse below the elbow, because the published low-smoothness hard laws use density support holes excluded by \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band}}\).  It also does not claim arbitrary-smoothness attainment, a higher-order correction, full banked-region containment, adaptive unknown-smoothness inference, or a density-induced slowdown.

statement_notes.justification: The deterministic exhaustive switch combines two proved instances of the same total cross-pair estimator without a transition remainder; direct optimizer minimization then converts its guarantee into the explicit elbow rates.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem remains restricted to \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pair}}\); below the elbow it is an attained upper benchmark rather than a positive-band minimax conclusion.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the upper half of the positive-band minimax result above the elbow and the upper half of the honest low-smoothness bracket.
